title: Hide-and-Seek in Trajectories: Discovering Failure Signals for VLA Runtime Monitoring
action_head: mixed: discrete action tokens (OpenVLA; embeddings averaged over all layers and DoF) and flow/diffusion action expert (pi0, pi0.5; hidden state before velocity head at the final denoising step)
methods: single-layer LSTM detector on windowed action embeddings
question: Can a failure detector trained only with trajectory-level success/failure labels learn to localize where failure begins, and beat uniform label propagation (SAFE) at multi-task failure detection on VLAs?
key_findings: LIBERO-10 OpenVLA (51.0% SR), bACC seen/unseen: Hide-and-Seek 0.852 / 0.834 vs SAFE-MLP 0.823 / 0.775 vs Cosine k-NN 0.758 / 0.639; token entropy/NLL baselines near chance (0.49-0.53) (Table 1, 3 seeds).
Real xArm 6 with pi0.5: CUBE bACC 0.966 seen / 0.914 unseen (SAFE-MLP 0.992 / 0.797); KITCHEN 0.968 / 0.972 (SAFE-MLP 0.784 / 0.878; LogpZO 0.895 / 0.837) (Table 3).

Uniform trajectory-label propagation under otherwise identical settings is worse by 19.4 bACC points on OpenVLA and 18.6 on pi0 (Fig. 4a); inter loss alone 0.825 / 0.856, intra alone 0.579 / 0.601, both 0.843 / 0.888 (Table 5).
Per-step MLP backbone is much worse than recurrent ones (OpenVLA 0.765 vs LSTM 0.843), so temporal context carries much of the signal (Table 4).

OpenVLA layer sweep (layers 0-31): no sharp peak; mid-to-late layers (20-31) slightly better, within about 3% bACC; layer-averaged features match or exceed the best single layer (85.2% seen, 83.4% unseen) (App. C.3).
A Qwen3-VL-8B video monitor reaches 0.712 bACC vs 0.843, at 2.343 s vs 0.001 s per step (Table 6).
Using the detector to pick the lowest-risk of N sampled pi0 action chunks raises held-out LIBERO-10 success from 83.4% to 87.4% (App. Table 12).

benchmarks: real xArm 6 CUBE and KITCHEN suites (4 tasks each)
evidence.scale: LIBERO-10: 500 episodes per policy (50 per task). Real: 98 success + 62 failure (CUBE), 102 + 58 (KITCHEN), 3 seen + 1 unseen task per suite. 3 random seeds; metrics averaged over alpha in {0.15, 0.20, 0.25}
evidence.statistics: partial: mean +/- std over 3 seeds in simulation; real-robot table has no std; no significance tests
evidence.baselines: 12 baselines: Mahalanobis, Cosine k-NN, PCA-KMeans, RND, LogpZO, cluster entropy, EigenScore, STAC, ACE, SAFE-LSTM, SAFE-MLP, token entropy/NLL (OpenVLA), uniform-label ablation, Qwen3-VL-8B monitor

causal_validation: None on internals. The only intervention is verifier-guided selection among sampled action chunks (appendix), which tests usefulness of the score, not what the embeddings represent.
closed_loop: Mainly offline detection on recorded rollouts. One closed-loop use in the appendix: best-of-N action-chunk selection with pi0 on held-out LIBERO-10 tasks (+4.0 points SR), seeds not reported for it.
limitations_stated: Averaging over the degree-of-freedom dimension may discard kinematic structure relevant to joint-specific failures.
Some failure modes are perceptual and may not be captured by action-level embeddings; visual features could be complementary.
Does not close the loop with correction, recovery or interaction; detectors can still give false negatives and false positives.
critique: A clear methodological improvement over SAFE's uniform labeling, but the gain over SAFE-MLP is modest in simulation (2-7 bACC points) with overlapping std on some splits.
Real-robot 'unseen' is a single held-out task per suite, so the strong unseen KITCHEN number (0.972) is one task; SAFE-MLP beats it on seen CUBE.
Failure-onset references for the timeliness plot are annotated by GPT-5.2 on videos (with a human-agreement check in the appendix), so 'detects near onset' depends on an LLM labeler.

No explicit guard is described in the parts read against episode-length shortcuts (LIBERO failures run to the time limit), which SAFE handled by truncation; the LSTM could partly exploit elapsed time.
The layer sweep is a useful negative result for mechanistic work: failure information in OpenVLA is spread across layers with no localized site.
code: project page referenced in the abstract (URL not given in the text)
one_line: Training an LSTM failure detector on VLA action embeddings with contrastive losses that find the most failure-like steps, instead of copying the trajectory label to every step, beats SAFE and 11 other baselines on OpenVLA, pi0 and pi0.5 in simulation and on a real arm.
